name: Seeed XIAO nRF52840 (and Sense)
radio: the SoC's own radio: ble (Bluetooth 5.0 / BLE; the 802.15.4 radio is unused)

flash.bootloader_instructions: Double-tap the reset button (the small button beside the USB-C port, or short RST to GND twice): the Adafruit nRF52 UF2 bootloader comes up as a drive named XIAO-SENSE. Copy the CircuitPython .uf2 from the board page onto it; the board reboots into CircuitPython and the CIRCUITPY drive appears. This page's UF2 copier knows the RP2040 bootloader only, so this one is a drag-and-drop from the file manager (a terminal is not needed).
flash.note: 2 MB QSPI flash beside the chip's 1 MB; the UF2 bootloader is on the board from the factory and survives everything but a J-Link erase. 256 KB RAM.

usb.when: CircuitPython CDC (Seeed's ids: the Sense and plain boards share the build and the pid)

pins.name: LED
pins.note: the red channel of the RGB user LED, P0.26, active low (board.LED is this pin in CircuitPython's build)

pins.name: VBATT
pins.note: battery divider output (1/3 of the cell), live only while READ_BATT_ENABLE is driven low

pins.name: READ_BATT_ENABLE
pins.note: drive low to connect the battery divider to VBATT (floating by default to save the cell)

pins.name: CHARGE_RATE
pins.note: low selects the 100 mA charge current, high (default) 50 mA

pins.name: CHARGE_STATUS
pins.note: low while the BQ25101 is charging

led.note: one RGB LED, three active-low lines; foxlib drives board.LED (the red channel). The firmware does not honour active_low yet, so the LED reads inverted (lit while the fox is off): note the direction on the bench. A separate orange charge LED is the charger's, not a GPIO.

battery.divider_note: BQ25101 charger with BAT pads on the back (3.7 V cell). A divider to VBATT (P0.31) is on the board, but it is switched: READ_BATT_ENABLE (P0.14) must be driven low to read it, which foxlib's battery role does not do, so roles.batt_sense stays null until it does.

notes: BLE only: the ble-beacon and puzzle-beacon templates. No Wi-Fi, no 5 GHz, no Wi-Fi checkpoint.
gpio numbers here are nRF port*32+pin (P1.11 = 43); CircuitPython names the pins D0..D10 and the roles above.
The Sense board adds an IMU and a PDM microphone (IMU_PWR, MIC_PWR are power-switch pins) and reports the same id; the plain board runs the same build.
An onboard ceramic antenna; no U.FL. NFC1/NFC2 (P0.09/P0.10) are the NFC antenna pads, not GPIO by default.

The nRF52 watchdog is one-way: once started it cannot be reconfigured or stopped, and a soft reboot does not clear it. After a deploy or reload the previous run's watchdog is still counting; foxlib 1.11.4 adopts it (banner: watchdog adopted(90s)). A board sitting at the REPL longer than limits.watchdog_s resets into safe mode, from which safemode.py restarts the fox; a power cycle starts clean. Keep bench phases short, or power-cycle between them.

circuitpython.note: One build for both boards (the Sense's page; Seeed's plain XIAO nRF52840 is listed as running the same firmware). The id is mixed-case as CircuitPython's board directory is: Seeed_XIAO_nRF52840_Sense. Installed as a .uf2 on the XIAO-SENSE bootloader drive, not from this page. board.LED is the red channel; LED_GREEN and LED_BLUE are the others. On the bench 2026-11-24: both BLE templates from .mpy, 73 KB free at the banner.
